source.section: Form 1 line 2c (PDF p10 Line 2c: 'age 65 or over before January 1, 2026'; spouse counted separately), lines 2a, 2g, 4, 10-22

worked: Federal AGI = private pension 50,000.00 (person 0) = 50,000.00 (given). Federal taxable income = 50,000.00 - 33,100.00 standard deduction (31,500.00 + 1 x 1,600.00 age 65 or older) = 16,900.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Massachusetts Form 1 (the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt items): Line 4 taxable pensions = 50,000.00 private pension (taxed: most private pensions are taxable, PDF p10) = 50,000.00. Line 10 total 5.0% income = 50,000.00. Line 16 total deductions = 0.00. Line 17 = 50,000.00 - 0.00 = 50,000.00. Line 2a personal exemption (married_joint) = 8,800.00; line 2c age 65 or over before 2026: 1 x 700.00 = 700.00; line 2g = line 18 = 9,500.00. Line 19 = 50,000.00 - 9,500.00 = 40,500.00. Line 20 interest and dividends = 0.00. Line 21 = 40,500.00. Line 22 = 40,500.00 x 0.05 = 2,025.00. No 8.5%/12% income or long-term gains (lines 23-24 = 0.00); 4% surtax 0.00 (line 21 is under 1,083,150). Line 28 total tax = 2,025.00; no credits (No Tax Status and the Limited Income Credit do not apply: Massachusetts AGI 50,000.00 is over their limits). State income tax = 2,025.00. Whose age counts: line 2c counts each person 65 or over before January 1, 2026; person 0 (born 1960-12-31) is 65 on December 31, 2025 and qualifies; person 1 (64) does not, so one 700.00 exemption.
